$comment: Hatsu's OWN workflow policy. This file is the policy half of the two-file configuration model documented in docs/WORKFLOW.md: nen/contract.json says what nen EXECUTES (lanes, argv, preconditions, hosts, targets), this file says what the workflow DECIDES with (branch shape, which declared verbs run per iteration, the coverage ladder, where reports go, which trailers a commit may carry, which model tier a persona gets). At the pinned nen 0.5.0 `nen schema check` VALIDATES this file -- an `ok nen/workflow.json` row, and a FAIL by pointer on a malformed key -- and two verbs read parts of it: `nen commit format --repo` takes `commits.allowedAttributionTrailers`, and `nen shu coverage --touched` takes the `coverage` ladder when no `--threshold` is given. Everything else here is read by the skills themselves, which is a read rather than a residue: nen validates this file, it does not hand the values out. Every value here is a policy default, not a fact about the machine.

branch.$comment: {model} is the MODEL ALIAS the actor runs on (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable), {persona} the roster persona it acts as, {descriptor} a short kebab noun phrase for the effort. Example: opus/kurapika/machinery-wave-1. `base` is the trunk breath fast-forwards, ao pulls from, and the PreToolUse hook refuses a commit or a push on.

iteration.$comment: The declared verbs rasengan runs before every commit. Hatsu is bash-and-markdown: its only mechanical check is `claude plugin validate . --strict`, declared as the `plugin` lane's `lint`. There is no build to run and no test suite to run, and both are seats in nen/contract.json saying so in the repository's own words.

tests.$comment: Hatsu ships no automated test suite; scripts/plugin_bump_check.sh is exercised by the recorded transcripts in docs/ab/plugin-bump-guard.md. tsukuyomi therefore has nothing to run here and says so rather than inventing a runner. An empty `required` is a statement, not an omission.

coverage.$comment: The ladder gyo reports against, in percent line coverage of TOUCHED files. Under `minimum` is a G5 stop, never a lowered bar. Hatsu declares no coverage verb, so gyo reports `not measurable here` against this ladder rather than a number — the ladder still ships because it is the policy every repository Hatsu drives inherits when it declares none of its own.

launch.$comment: Hatsu has no runnable application: it is a plugin read by Claude Code. amaterasu names that fact and launches nothing. A repository with launch targets names them in nen/contract.json under project.launch and selects one here.

reports.$comment: `dir` is git-ignored (.gitignore). `retain: final-only` governs what is KEPT, not whether a working file exists (maintainer's ruling, 2026-09-09): only the final post-merge report gets a dated file of its own under `dir`, and the per-turn and landing reports are published to the conversation as an Artifact -- or, on a surface that cannot publish one, opened from the TRANSIENT `<dir>/current.html`, which every render overwrites and git ignores. One always-latest working file is not a retained report. `template` names templates/<name>.html in this repository.

notifications.$comment: jutaisho's ladder, innermost first: `push` is the surface's own turn-complete signal, `os` an osascript notification, `sound` /System/Library/Sounds/<sound>.aiff through afplay. hooks/stop-bell.sh rings rungs 2 and 3 off .nen/last-stop.json; a rung absent from this list is not rung. `turn` decides how loud an ORDINARY turn is -- one with no gate: `rung1` (the default, and what an absent key reads as) rings only the first rung `rungs` lists, `all` rings every rung it lists. A GATE always rings everything `rungs` lists regardless of `turn`, and `turn` can only WITHHOLD an escalation `rungs` already grants -- it can never conjure a rung `rungs` does not list. nen reads and validates this key from v0.5.0 -- a closed set of `rung1` and `all`, refused by pointer on anything else -- and fires none of the three rungs itself; hooks/stop-bell.sh is what rings them.

commits.$comment: TWO PROVENANCE TRAILERS, ONE PER PLANE -- the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-10, refining the ruling of 2026-09-09. `Hatsu-Agent: <persona>` is what a LOCAL Hatsu session writes: Kurapika and the independents, on the maintainer's own credentials. `Akatsuki-Agent: <persona>` belongs to the AUTONOMOUS CI PLANE (zheref/akatsuki-ai) and is written only by an Akatsuki roster agent there. BOTH KEYS ARE ADMITTED HERE so that one commit-msg hook passes a commit from either plane; ADMITTING A KEY IS NOT LICENCE TO WRITE IT -- a local persona writes `Hatsu-Agent` and REFUSES to write `Akatsuki-Agent`, because a persona is not the CI plane and writing it would forge a machine-plane provenance this plane does not have. Neither key is AI attribution: each names the system's OWN provenance -- which agent of which plane did the work -- rather than a model claiming authorship, which is exactly why they are the only two admitted and no other AI attribution trailer is ever recorded. Commits already on `main` carrying the old key are NOT rewritten; they are the record of what was written then. A harness that would mandate `Co-Authored-By:` must be turned off as a SETUP STEP -- `includeCoAuthoredBy: false` in ~/.claude/settings.json -- which is a thing to check rather than a thing this file can assert; docs/WORKFLOW.md § commits carries the check. ENFORCEMENT IS THREE-LAYERED AND ONLY THE FIRST LAYER SHIPS IN THIS PLUGIN: (a) the skills refuse to WRITE a forbidden trailer -- kokusen before it commits, aka before it squashes -- which is agent-side, and from 2026-09-10 layer (a) ALSO carries the refusal to write `Akatsuki-Agent` from a local session, ALONE: (b) and (c) admit that key by construction and cannot make this distinction; (b) the target repository's commit-msg hook, which `nen scaffold init` generates from `allowedAttributionTrailers` (KroApple and kro-pwa carry one); (c) `nen commit format --repo` and `nen wc squash` refusing the trailer outright. AT THE PINNED NEN 0.5.0 LAYER (c) IS INSTALLED wherever the invocation carries `--repo`: verified live against this checkout, `nen commit format --repo . --trailer Co-Authored-By=someone` exits 2 naming this file and the keys it admits, while `--trailer Hatsu-Agent=kurapika` renders at exit 0. LAYER (b) STAYS TARGET-DEPENDENT -- this repository is not scaffolded with the hook -- so a raw `git commit --file` carrying `Co-Authored-By` is still not mechanically refused HERE. Say which layers the repository in front of you actually has, rather than claiming a guard that is not installed.

monitor.$comment: en's izanagi cap and its poll interval. The cap is grammar, not a default: a watch loop with no cap does not run.

models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: Cursor-native only; provider models there are reserved for Bugbot

models.$comment: A tier is named, never a model version — a pinned version is a pin that rots. The orchestrator tier is the main session's; a SUBAGENT never runs on it, because the frontier tier is where the human's own conversation lives and a delegate that outranks its caller has inverted the delegation.
